The next import of app.services.price_service therefore builds a FRESH module object, and the package attribute app.services.price_service is rebound to it.

app/services/structured_comparison_service.py:1196-1247 binds fetch_shopify_price BY NAME at its own import. At that point scs was already imported, at collection of our file. So scs keeps the OLD function object, whose __globals__ is the orphaned OLD module dict. fetch_shopify_price (price_service.py:15375) resolves `_fetch_shopify_catalog` through its __globals__. The fixture's `from app.services import price_service` + patch.object stubbed the NEW module. The OLD function never saw the stub, so the real catalog fetch ran and hit curl_cffi, and the socket guard recorded 3 hosts x 2 per node.

The noon stub held because it patches scs.fetch_noon_price, which is looked up in scs's own globals.

fix:W4-9-r2.pr_text:
**CI hermeticity note, round 2.** The second CI run no longer showed the Serper leak; round 1's `_serper_unconfigured` fixture holds. It still failed the same two nodes at the socket-guard teardown. This time the cause was 6 curl_cffi fetches of `<host>/products.json` (en-bh.ajmal.com, alhajisbahrain.com, bh.asgharali.com), even though the fixture stubs `price_service._fetch_shopify_catalog`.

The failure depends on test order, not on the product code. `tests/test_platform_router.py::test_does_not_import_price_service` deletes `app.services.price_service` from `sys.modules` to prove there is no import cycle. The next import therefore builds a fresh module object. `structured_comparison_service` still holds the `fetch_shopify_price` it imported by name, and that function looks up `_fetch_shopify_catalog` in the orphaned old module's globals. So the stub was set on the new module and never reached the code the orchestrator runs. The noon stub held because it patches `scs` directly.

Reproduced locally with just that one test followed by this file (2 errors, identical to CI); the file passes alone. The fix is in the test file only. The fixture now sets the Shopify stub, with per-key monkeypatch restore, in every `price_service` module dict the code can reach: the live `sys.modules` entry, plus the `__globals__` of every `fetch_shopify_price` bound in a loaded module. That makes it hold whether the module was reloaded (one dict) or re-imported fresh (two dicts).

Verified:
- The reproduction order, the round-1 order, the neighbouring files and a reload variant all pass.
- A mutant that patches only the live module brings the 2 errors back.
- The first 583 files of CI's order plus this file, run locally with CI's deselects, show no failure in this file (the 5 unrelated failures are explained in the round-2 report).
- The socket guard's assertion is unchanged.
follow_up: tests/test_platform_router.py::test_does_not_import_price_service (lines 317-328) deletes every price_service entry from sys.modules and never restores the original module. After it runs, any module that bound price_service names at import (structured_comparison_service, and test files that `from app.services.price_service import ...` at collection) calls functions whose globals are an orphaned module dict. Patching `app.services.price_service` then silently misses them. Measured victim: tests/test_shopify_discovery_l13.py::TestFetchShopifyPrice::test_fetch_uses_catalog_and_matches. It imports fetch_shopify_price by name at line 24-26 and monkeypatches the re-imported `ps` at line 194. Alone it passes with 0 egress. After the platform_router node, it makes 3 real curl_cffi GETs to https://shopalmoayyed.com/products.json and, under a guard, fails `assert None is not None`. In CI (unguarded) it PASSED at position 488 after platform_router at 364. So in CI it most likely reached the live store and passed on the live catalog, which is a hidden live-network dependency. Suggested fix: run the cycle proof in a subprocess, or snapshot and restore sys.modules (and the app.services.price_service package attribute) in a try/finally. This is a separate issue from #183 (the Serper reload leak) and #184 (the curl_cffi guard gap), though #184's conftest-level curl guard would turn it from silent egress into a visible failure.

The other `fetch_*` stubs in this repo that patch price_service by module attribute while the code under test binds by name have the same exposure after that test runs. A repo-wide grep for `patch.object(price_service,` / `monkeypatch.setattr(ps,` combined with by-name imports of the patched function's callers would size it.
